chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed altogether, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Habib ibn Bishr, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: No, by Allah! There is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than Taqiyya (dissimulation/prudence). O Habib! Indeed, whoever has Taqiyya, Allah will elevate him. O Habib! Whoever does not have Taqiyya, Allah will place him down. O Habib! The people are merely in a truce (of hostilities); so if that (hostilities) had been there, this (Taqiyya) would be there.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyya (prudent dissimulation or concealment of faith)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyya in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, underscores Taqiyya not merely as a defensive tactic but as a spiritual elevation mechanism, reflecting the Imams' strategic navigation of political instability. The reference to 'hudna' (truce) highlights the transitional nature of the current era, where concealment preserves the community until the conditions for open manifestation are met. This aligns with the Shia jurisprudential view that Taqiyya is a means of maintaining religious integrity and social cohesion under duress.
